description: The plot illustrates how accuracy varies with different values of “o_pop frequency (x10^4)” for two series labeled “Initial Accuracy” and “Final Accuracy.” The x-axis is labeled “o_pop frequency (x10^4)” on a linear scale, spanning from 1 to 19 with tick marks at 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, and 19. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” on a linear scale from 0.0 to 1.0, with regularly spaced tick labels at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0. The “Initial Accuracy” line is green with square markers connected by a solid line and includes vertical error bars; it starts near 0.34 at x=1, rises to about 0.48 at x=5, drops to around 0.28 at x=7, increases to roughly 0.52 at x=13, then declines to about 0.36 at x=17 and ends near 0.40 at x=19. The “Final Accuracy” line is blue with circular markers connected by a dashed line and includes vertical error bars; it begins around 0.65 at x=1, increases to about 0.86 at x=5, dips to roughly 0.72 at x=7, peaks near 0.92 at x=9, falls to around 0.69–0.70 at x=11–13, rises again to about 0.90 at x=15, dips to about 0.82 at x=17, and ends near 0.90 at x=19.
